CMI.thesis_one_line: Engine and data-center power-systems maker with a real structural tailwind, but the price already assumes growth well above what it has ever delivered.
kill_criteria: EBITDA margin stays below 18.0% for two consecutive quarters despite reiterated FY26 guidance (would break the "raises are backed by margin" thesis).
Power Systems / large-genset book-to-bill falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (backlog thesis breaking).
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x (from ~0.6x) without offsetting FCF growth.
NTM P/E re-rates above the 20x peer median without a corresponding upward revision to consensus 10-year growth.
Follow-on shareholder/consumer litigation tied to the 2023-24 DOJ/EPA/CARB Clean Air Act settlement produces a material (>$200M) incremental charge beyond current accruals.
key_adverse_facts: Q2-26 EBITDA margin fell YoY (17.5% vs 18.4%) despite three consecutive guidance raises, driven by higher incentive comp and R&D.

Q1-24 GAAP EPS of $14.03 included a one-off $1.3bn ($9.08/share) Atmus divestiture gain; Q4-25 GAAP results included a $458M ($3.28/share) mostly non-cash Electrolyzer/Accelera charge - both must be excluded from any 'clean' trend read.
$1.675bn DOJ/EPA/CARB Clean Air Act settlement (finalized Apr-2024) remains subject to ongoing shareholder/consumer follow-on litigation.
V1 reverse DCF implies the price already discounts 15.66%/yr FCF growth for 10 years vs 8.4-8.9% consensus/delivered growth; V1 base-case 3y annualised return is negative (-3.9%).
data_conflicts: Sell-side mean price target ($746) and even the low target ($530) sit above the $525.06 close, implying Street consensus is more bullish than V1's reverse DCF (verdict 'excessive', base case -3.9%/yr) - an unresolved disagreement between two legitimate valuation approaches, flagged rather than resolved.
Triage attributed V1's 'excessive' flag to price momentum; the flag is actually a fundamentals-based reverse-DCF result independent of the momentum factor - triage's causal claim is not supported.
CMI.confidence_in_thesis: medium - quality and the structural data-center driver are well evidenced, but the valuation math is the swing factor and depends on assumptions (WACC, terminal growth) that are inherently uncertain

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: This dossier agrees with V1: the reverse DCF implies growth (15.7%/yr) well above delivered/consensus (8-9%), and V1's own base-case 3y return is already negative; the durable data-center tailwind is real but insufficient to close this gap at the current price.

BRO.thesis_one_line: Insurance broker whose headline growth is now mostly a debt-funded mega-acquisition, while underlying organic growth just turned negative.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth negative for 3+ consecutive quarters (1 of 3 so far: Q2-26).
Adjusted EBITDAC margin contracts >150bps YoY for two consecutive quarters (Q2-26 was already -100bps YoY).
Accession-segment synergies fall short of the disclosed $30-40M FY26 target.
Additional material producer/team departures or adverse non-compete litigation rulings beyond the $18M already disclosed.
key_adverse_facts: Organic revenue growth decelerated for 5 straight quarters and turned negative in Q2-26 (-0.7%), after +6.5% in Q1-25; triage's '32% revenue growth' headline is almost entirely the debt/equity-funded Accession acquisition, not organic.

GAAP diluted EPS declined YoY in 3 of the last 5 quarters (Q2-25 -10%, Q3-25 -16%) as acquisition financing costs and an 18% increase in diluted share count outran GAAP net income growth; only adjusted EPS shows consistent (decelerating) growth.
Net debt/adjusted EBITDAC rose from well under 1x to roughly 2.8x to fund the $9.825bn Accession acquisition (Aug-2025).
$18M of Q2-26 revenue was lost to litigation tied to producers/staff departing for a competing startup.
Triage's '54% EPS growth' claim is not supported by GAAP or adjusted quarterly EPS found in SEC filings/press releases this session.
data_conflicts: Triage's growth narrative (32% revenue/54% EPS growth, 'proven broker compounder') conflicts with the primary-source organic-growth and GAAP-EPS trend, which shows deceleration into negative organic growth by Q2-26; this dossier's verdict is more cautious than triage's implied framing.
BRO.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low - valuation cross-checks agree the stock isn't priced for perfection, but the organic-growth deceleration is a live, unresolved trend, not yet a proven bottom

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation exists for BRO this cycle (absent from v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json); this dossier's own reverse-DCF and multiple cross-checks stand alone and are not reconciled against V1.

CMS.thesis_one_line: Michigan's dominant regulated utility with a 20-year dividend-growth streak and guidance never cut, but Moody's just flagged its huge capital plan as a credit risk.
kill_criteria: Moody's or S&P actually downgrades CMS Energy or Consumers Energy (current status: negative outlook only, ratings affirmed).
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($3.83-3.90) is cut mid-year (reaffirmed twice through Q2-26 to date).
An MPSC rate-case order disallows a material (>10%) share of pending capital-recovery requests.
Net debt continues rising without a matching credit-rating cushion or explicit securitization pass-through disclosure.
Adjusted EPS growth falls outside the reaffirmed 6-8% long-term range for two consecutive fiscal years.
key_adverse_facts: Q2-26 adjusted EPS missed consensus by >50% ($0.37 vs ~$0.76 expected) on weather, storm O&M, and non-repeating 2025 liability-management benefits; full-year guidance was reaffirmed the same day.
Moody's moved CMS Energy/Consumers Energy to a negative outlook (~March 2026) over the size of a $24bn five-year capital plan relative to regulatory cost-recovery timing.
Leverage is securitization-heavy (~6.3x per triage data card); net debt ~$18.8bn against modest TTM operating income, making headline ratios hard to compare cleanly to less-securitized peers.
FCF is structurally negative (capex materially exceeds OCF), a normal utility feature but one that rules out a standard FCF-yield valuation.
data_conflicts: None material found versus the quant/triage view this session; triage's characterisation (cheap NTM P/E, above-average guided growth, leverage 'typical not new concern') is corroborated by primary-source guidance history, though the Moody's negative-outlook action (not in the triage card) is a genuine incremental risk this dossier adds.
CMS.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high - the guidance track record is strong and independently verified across 4 releases; the main uncertainty is credit-rating trajectory, not the earnings algorithm

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation exists for CMS this cycle (absent from v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json); this dossier's reverse dividend-discount cross-check (implied growth ~5.2%, below the guided 6-8% algorithm) stands alone and supports a fair-to-cheap read.
